blocks.text: SYDNEY — Drone patrols in New South Wales detected an average of 20 sharks a day at patrolled beaches over winter as aerial surveillance is ramped up for the school holidays. Drone operators detected 1,225 sharks from July 1 to August 31, according to newly released data. The sightings prompted 360 shark safety measures, including evacuating people from the water, sounding alarms to alert swimmers and surfers, and deploying inflatable boats and jet skis.
